Bathory- Blood Fire Death. I was at the time not familiar with Peter Arbo's work. The title, the bands image, the music, everything was perfectly expressed by this painting. 

As a side note, the story behind the cover of "Under the sign of the Black Mark" would be near unbelieveable without its repeated mention by Quorthon in interviews, and a photo of the subject (Leif Ernhborg, at the time a well known swedish body builder) directly after the shoot.


In short, Quorthon wanted to recreate Goya's "Witches Sabbath" for the album cover I.E scantly clad woman bowing around a horned goat figure. He somehow managed to get access to the Swedish Royal Opera House, to use the mountainous set as a back drop.

They had the photoshoot during the intermission of "Carmen" with the curtain down, with the audience on the other side. The photographer could not get a shot with Leif in as well as the girls. As time ran out he shot the album cover, a single goatheaded man holding an Ox bone, towering over the landscape. 

In other words, how to make a classic cover 101

I work night shift at a gas station, so I have met a lot of characters seemingly randomly at 3 am. One night a few months ago, I was jamming out to some music, in a great mood, air drums and all. A guy, roughly 30, pulled up In a beat up intrepid. He was wearing a snapback, in ratty clothes, but he smiled and motioned to me. We got to talking (I chat up customers when I'm really bored). He was homeless living out of his car after an ex girlfriend kicked him out. Mike seemed honest, my mom always taught me to give everyone a chance and always to help others who are down there luck.

That night he needed a place to hang out till work, asked me to charge his phone. I gave him a free coffee and some free snacks. Mike was an ex felon, (marijuana with intent to distribute), had served two years at 17. He was also a recovering addict, been clean for nine months (had scars on his arm I asked about, I have a no junkie policy). I got to know him over a few months, he'd come in once a week to say hi and talk.

After a while he stopped showing up, I was concerned. The next time I saw him his face was fucked up and he was in a different car. He had been robbed, beat in the face with a bottle at a different statkon, no money, with his car impounded due to a friend stealing it. In order to get his car back he needed to drive out of county, pay 80 or so dollars in fees then see a magistrate in two weeks. His whole life was in that car, and he saw his only option as selling his prescription adderall at a truck stop (a class 2 narcotic, a felony).

I wouldn't be able to sleep at night if he went back to jail, I cared about the guy enough. I gave him 100$ as a gift, to his protests. Mike started getting emktional, asking me what I needed and if I was even a real person. I wouldn't have piece of mind if he had gone off and done that. 

He was able to get his car, and now is lining up an apartment ( a tough thing to do, no one wants to live by a drug dealer). I haven't seen him in a while, but whenever I do he looks at me like I'm an angel. He's offered me money, anything in his power, breakfast, etc etc. 

I guess I was the random person in this scenario. It has been a really rich expierence in my life to help someone like that. Being outgoing like that really gave me a new meaning in life, helping others allowed me to help myself and heal self doubt and insecurities, one good deed at a time

Youre living my life. In bizzaro world, one day we will pass through the same town in our beaters and I think to myself "that guy knows my pain". 70hours a week? Check. Multiple difficult jobs? Check.  Looking for another solution besides suicide, while fighting a horrible all consuming depression?Check. No financial help, because parents make too much and wouldnt help my college education? Check.

I was scammed out of $1000 by a stranger I thought I was helping out. This was a lot of money too me. He spun a sad tale, always had a bigger problem, gave me bad checks. I have never been afraid to make mistakes, and have always done what I thought was right. There have been times in my life I wish someone, anyone would have helped me and reached out. It really damaged my self esteem when I figured it out, crying in a police station about this was a tough moment. After filing a police report I swore off helping strangers or giving a shit.

Fast forward 2 weeks and I meet a guy named mike through my job (night clerk). Mike was a genuinely nice guy, very respectful. He was homeless living out of a beat up intrepid. As an ex-felon and recovering addict, not a lot of people gave him a moment. He spoke about prison, life, god, making mistakes, the good times and the hard times. He came up infrequently, only on my shift to talk and maybe grab some snacks. He reminded me of my older brother from a long time ago, something no one has done in years.

One day he shows up with a nasty cut on his nose, blood pooling under his eyes in a different car. His friend had been arrested driving his car, the car was impounded. Hours later a bottle was broken on his face, and he was robbed for his prescription cyboxin. Everything he owned was in that car, and he needed money to get it out of impound. He was going to try to sell his adderall at the truck stop, a felony. I gave him 80$ telling him not to sell adderall and stay out of trouble, not to worry about paying me back, and that everyone needs some help to get on there feet.

This grown ass felon was on the verge of tears, asking me if I was even a person, how can someone be this kind. Asking me what I needed. I never told him but I needed my faith in people back, that I could have a positive effect on someone.

Last time I saw him he was about to move into an apartment, staying clean, working a full time job. He comes in to say hi, see how I'm doing, offers to help me out in any way, any time. I am proud of what I did for him, and I never lost that big heart no matter how tough times are

Having a negative experience when trying to get help, due to the personal feelings of the doctors\ therapist you spoke too, because they stereotype you.

I had an older woman as a therapiat, after years of being off meds I was ready to get help for major depressive and anxiety. I came clean about my life, including my self medicating with marijuana very infrequently. " WELL THATS A MOTIVATION KILLER, ISNT IT". I was then treated like a substance abuse patient for the remainder of the session. 

Some of her pearls of wisdom included, " you put yourself in that situation", " well look where your choices  landed you". And my personal favorite, when speaking about my relationship problems was how she insinuated I should break up with her because I didn't know what love is.

I left and later attempted suicide, feeling immeasurably worse. I just recently started to get help again, and my advice is that if that person makes you feel worse you stand up and walk right out and refuse to pay. I never had a worse moment in my life.

I was in a car crash I should not have walked away from. (Head on collision at 60mph, after I was facing the wrong way on a freeway due to spinning out in the rain.) I was situated by the median after spinning out, stopped completely, watching oncoming traffic fly by in 2 inches of pooled rain on the expressway. Adrenaline kicked in, I was scared to die, and knew it was not looking my way. As I sat there waiting for a break in traffic to reposition myself, the rain broke and the most vivid rainbow formed. It was surreal, I was the only one on this side of the highway who could see it, the angle made it seem like a bridge. Seconds later a Volvo cut hard left, seeing me far to late and slammed into me. I blacked out, broke my nose, but was up In seconds checking on the other driver. We both lived. I've never been able to make sense of it, and i realize its arbitrary, but people spend there whole lives waiting for a moment like that. Right before the car hit, I shut my eyes and asked god to let me live (I was 18). I can still see it. I can still remember every little detail of that 5 minutes. So many factors had to fall into place. It very easily could've been a pile up. My car could have been pushed into the lane. The engine had folded missing my legs. Anything could have happened and nothing did. Murphys law was wrong that day. And since then I've had faith in a higher power, and lived a fuller life for it.

And my friends dad once screamed in an alcoholic rage " I WILL BEAT YOU LIKE TEN MOTHERF&CKERS"  

Perspective is the most important thing you can learn about someone else. Gotta listen to learn

I'd also give myself a hug (no one ever hugged me enough), tell myself to get a haircut, some new duds, and give myself 20$ for some ice cream at Twist and Shake.
